intended_object: The semantics of Metamath's proper substitution `[ x / y ] ph` (substitute the variable x for y in ph). In a structure S under an assignment v, it holds exactly when ph holds under the assignment v[y ↦ v(x)]. This comes from the docstring and from how the definition is used in `df_clab_semantics`/`valid_df_clab`.
explanation:
By the Metamath convention, `[ x / y ] ph` means "ph with x put in place of y". By the substitution lemma, it is satisfied under v exactly when ph is satisfied under v updated so that y takes the value v x. The body, `Wff.Holds S (update v y (v x)) p`, says exactly this.

The library checks this against its other notions:
- `df_clab_semantics` proves that `x ∈ {y | ph}` holds iff `CvSubstHolds S v x y p`, which is the df-clab axiom.
- `valid_df_clab` then connects it to the `SubstHolds` / `sbDefiniens` form (df-sb). There, `SubstHolds S v x y p` unfolds to the same `update v y (v x)` expression, so the two agree.

The degenerate case x = y also works: the update is then the identity, so the definition reduces to ph holding under v, as it should.

This is the satisfaction clause of the library's own fixed syntax (`Wff` over the language `LNF`), so no broader generality applies here. Mathlib's `FirstOrder.Language` substitution belongs to a different framework and is not the same declaration.
